name: Glacial-Vestment
geological_features: Subsurface ocean heated by tidal forces
Ice geysers driven by subsurface pressure
specific_features: Ice sheet layers that drape the surface like folded fabric
Large marine fauna that breach through thin ice to access the atmosphere
description: Glacial-Vestment is a large ice world wrapped in ice sheets so extensive and layered that from orbit they appear as draped fabric, the compression folds and flow patterns creating textures that resemble the heavy vestments of some planetary-scale garment. The high gravity compresses the ice into dense, blue-tinted layers of remarkable clarity, each stratum recording atmospheric conditions at the time of its deposition. A subsurface ocean, heated by tidal forces from the gas giant this world orbits, circulates beneath the ice in a global current system that drives the ice geysers erupting through thinner portions of the frozen crust.

The dense atmosphere retains heat more effectively than the ice-world average, keeping surface temperatures in a range that, while bitterly cold, permits sustained surface operations with standard cold-weather equipment rather than the full environmental suits required on thinner-atmosphere ice worlds. The ice geysers erupt with dramatic force, the pressurized subsurface water blasting through kilometers of ice to reach the surface, where it freezes instantly into towering pillars and arcs of new ice. The marine fauna of the subsurface ocean occasionally breach through thin ice, their massive bodies breaking the surface to exchange respiratory gases with the dense atmosphere above.

The breaching fauna are among the largest organisms documented on any world, some exceeding eighty meters in length, their bodies insulated by thick layers of blubber-analog tissue and powered by metabolisms adapted to the high-gravity, cold-water environment. Their breaching behavior is essential, the subsurface ocean lacking sufficient dissolved oxygen to sustain their metabolic needs, requiring them to surface periodically through maintained breathing holes in the ice. The ecosystem below the ice is extensive, supported by chemosynthetic organisms around the tidal heating vents, and the breaching megafauna represent the apex of a food chain that extends from microbial mats to predators of extraordinary size.

Deuterium extraction from the subsurface ocean is a growing industry, the tidal heating maintaining liquid water access through natural channels that reduce the energy cost of drilling. The biological compounds produced by the deep-ocean organisms have medical and industrial applications under active investigation. The primary operational challenge is the ice itself, which shifts and reforms constantly under glacial pressure, closing access channels and threatening surface installations with slow but unstoppable advance. Workers on Glacial-Vestment learn to treat the ice as a living adversary, patient and powerful, that gives ground reluctantly and takes it back the moment attention lapses.
